input.task: What does the export button say?

provenance: PR #60 R12: the `/`-escape shipped in round 1 with NO case that could go red. The reviewer deleted the `.replace("/", ...)` call and ran the whole gate — `invariant` 77/77 and `fast` 227/227, both green with the fix removed — and the widened round-trip check that had found the crash now lists `button` in `resolve_advertised_except`, which is the role carrying the offending name, so the suite could not reach it by construction. This case reaches it directly. Playwright serialises a regex `name=` into its own `/…/flags` selector literal, so an unescaped slash terminates the literal and `get_by_role` raises `InvalidSelectorError` — which `classify` reads as `act`, i.e. a page-content-dependent crash misdiagnosed as an action failure. The button's label is uppercased by stylesheet, so the exact pass finds nothing and the FOLDED pass — the only one that builds a regex — is what runs. A sweep of the other special characters through the role tier found no sibling, so one case covers it.

triage.note: Role tier specifically: `get_by_text` with the same pattern returns count 1 and does not crash, so a text-tier case would grade nothing. `trace_note_contains` is asserted too, because a case that stopped reaching the folded pass would otherwise pass for the wrong reason.
